calibration.surprise_note: Predicted 0.4 success; realized rejection matched the top predeclared failure mode. The surprise was magnitude and mechanism: episode duration, not entry quality, drives the loss - long bears convert one trigger into 50-124 sequential re-entries, so per-trade edge is dominated by episode-length exposure. Any retry must budget entries per episode or condition on bear-vs-correction state, which is a different gate shape.

hypothesis: Deep index drawdown episodes (QQQ close >=12% below rolling 252d high) followed by a first stabilization day (up close finishing in the upper half of the daily range) predict positive 5-day forward ETF rebound; next-open entry, fixed 5-day hold, default-off paper ETF sleeve with pre-2023 index history backfill as new evidence.
new_evidence_type: new data source (pre-2023 index daily history, not in warehouse) + new gate shape (index-drawdown episode trigger vs unconditional scan)
notes: Deep-drawdown 'buy the first stabilization day' is structurally a falling-knife policy in secular bears: the -12%/-5% hysteresis episode stays active for years while the 252d rolling high decays, so the sleeve re-enters every bounce (124 re-entries in the dot-com bear). Correction-type episodes (14 of 17) were mildly positive (+$5777, 11/14 positive), but the predeclared bundle cannot distinguish correction from bear onset ex ante, and slicing that after the fact would be a post-hoc retune. Evidence assets kept: data/non_ohlcv/index_history archive (new durable source), quant/deep_drawdown_rebound_paper_sleeve.py + tests, replay artifact data/experiments/exp-20260706-003/.

post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: A legitimate retry needs a genuinely different gate shape declared up front: a predeclared per-episode entry budget (e.g. first stabilization only), or an ex-ante bear-vs-correction conditioning state (e.g. PIT regime classifier risk_off vs chop, or 200d-slope filter) fixed BEFORE replay; or new settled forward rows from a live episode. The pre-2023 index archive (data/non_ohlcv/index_history) is durable and reusable for that follow-up without re-fetching.
